44:1: Its meaning has already been explained in his saying: “Ha Meem. By the clear Book.”
44:3: And His saying: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. God Almighty swore by this book, that He sent it down during a blessed night. The interpreters of the Qur’an differed regarding that night, which night of the year it was. Some of them said: It is the Night of Decree. It was mentioned that he said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, meaning the Night of Decree. The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramadan, the Torah was sent down six nights before Ramadan, the Psalms were sent down sixteen nights before Ramadan, the Gospel was sent down eighteen nights before Ramadan, and the Criterion was sent down twenty-four nights before Ramadan. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: On a blessed night, he said: It is the Night of Decree. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God Almighty: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn.” He said: That night is the Night of Decree. God sent down this Qur’an from the Mother of the Book on the Night of Decree, then He sent it down to the prophets during the nights and days, and on other than the Night of Decree. Others said: Rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban. The correct statement about this is the statement of those who said: It refers to the Night of Decree, because God Almighty has informed us that this is the case, as He, the Most High, said: Indeed, We were to warn. We created this Book that We sent down on the blessed night, so that Our punishment would befall those among them who disbelieved and did not turn to Our Oneness and the singularity of divinity for Us.
44:4: And His statement: In it every wise matter is decided. The people of interpretation differed regarding this night in which every wise matter is decided, similar to their difference regarding the blessed night. This is because the ha in His statement: In it refers back to the blessed night. Some of them said: It is the Night of Decree, in which the affairs of the entire year are decided: who dies, who is born, who is honored, who is humiliated, and all the other affairs of the year. It was mentioned that he said that: Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said: I was with Al-Hasan, and a man said to him: O Abu Saeed, is the Night of Decree in every Ramadan? He said: Yes, by God, it is in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is decided, in which God decrees every term, hope, and provision until its like. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Rabia bin Kulthum told us, he said: A man said to Al-Hasan while I was listening: Tell me about the Night of Decree, is it in every Ramadan? He said: Yes, by God, besides whom there is no god, it is in every Ramadan, and it is the night in which every wise matter is decreed, and God decrees every term, creation, and provision until its like. Yunus told me, he said Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abdul Hamid bin Salim said, on the authority of Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, he said: It is said that the Angel of Death copies the death of whoever dies on the Night of Decree to the same night, and that is because God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night and He said: Therein is decreed every precise matter. He said: So you will find a man marrying women and planting crops while his name is among the dead. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding his statement: Therein is distinguished every wise matter, he said: The matter of the year to the year is what it was of creation, sustenance, life span, calamity, or something like this. He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, who said: It was said: Wait for the judgment in the month of Ramadan. Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Saeed bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman, regarding his statement: Therein every wise matter is decreed, he said: The affairs of the year are managed on the Night of Decree. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Therein is decreed every matter of wisdom, he said: On the Night of Decree every matter that will happen from year to year: life and death, all livelihoods and calamities are decreed on it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night the Night of Decree in which every precise matter is distinguished. We used to say that in it the matter of one year is distinguished from the next. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It is the Night of Decree, in which whatever happens from one year to the next is decreed. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated from Mansur, who said: I asked Mujahid, saying: What do you think of the supplication of one of us, saying: O God, if my name is among the happy ones, then make it among them, and if it is among the wretched ones, then erase it from them and make him among the happy ones? He said: Good! Then I met him a year or more later and asked him about this supplication. He said: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn. * On that night is made distinct every matter of wisdom.” He said: On the Night of Decree, He decrees whatever provision or calamity will occur in the year, then He advances what He wills and delays what He wills. As for the decree of happiness and wretchedness, it is fixed and cannot be changed. Others said: Rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha’ban. It was mentioned that he said that: Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah and Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Al-Hasan bin Ismail Al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Suqah, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Therein is made distinct every matter of wisdom, he said: On the night of the middle of Sha’ban, the matter of the year is decided, the living are copied from the dead, and the pilgrims are written down, and no one is added to them, and no one is subtracted from them. Ubayd ibn Adam ibn Abi Iyas told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Aqil ibn Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Al-Mughirah ibn Al-Akhns, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Deaths are cut off from Sha’ban to Sha’ban, to the point that a man marries and has a child born to him, and his name has already been recorded among the dead.’” Muhammad ibn Muammar told me, he said: Abu Hisham told us, he said: Abdul Wahid told us, he said: Uthman ibn Hakim told us, he said: Saeed ibn Jubayr told us, he said: Ibn Abbas said: A man walks among the people while he has been raised up among the dead. He said: Then he recited this verse: “Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn. * In it is distinguished every precise matter.” He said: Then he said: In it, the matter of this world is distinguished from one year to another. The more correct of the two opinions is the one that says: That is the Night of Decree, based on what we have previously explained about the meaning of His statement, Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night, which is the Night of Decree, and the ha in His statement, therein is from the mention of the blessed night. What is meant by His statement, therein is decreed every precise matter is that on this blessed night every matter that God has decreed in that year is decided and determined for the next year. He put wise in place of decisive, as He said, “Alif, Lam, Meem. These are the verses of the Wise Book” (Luqman 1-2), meaning: decisive.
44:5: And His saying: “A command from Us. Indeed, We were sending messengers.” God Almighty says: On this blessed night, every wise matter is decreed, a command from Us. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement: Amrana. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is accusative because We sent it down as a command and a mercy in the state of Alif Laa `anzal We have sent it down as a command and a mercy.” Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It means that He separates every command into a division and a command.
44:6: He said: And likewise his saying: A mercy from your Lord. He said: It is permissible for mercy to be made accusative by the occurrence of messengers upon it, so mercy was made for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: Indeed, We were messengers means, the Most High said: Indeed, We were sending Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Our servants as a mercy from your Lord, O Muhammad. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing means: Indeed, God, Blessed and Exalted be He, is the All-Hearing of what these polytheists say regarding what We have sent down of Our Book, and what We have sent of Our Messengers to them, and other than that of their speech and the speech of others. He is the All-Knowing of what their hearts contain, and other than that of their affairs and the affairs of others.
44:7: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Lord of the heavens and the earth. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as <Lord of the heavens>in the nominative case, following the i’rab of al-Samee’ al-Aleem. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and some of the reciters of Mecca read it as Lord of the heavens is a lowering in response to the Lord in His Almighty’s saying, A mercy from your Lord. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whoever recites them is correct. What is meant by his saying: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them is that God Almighty says, He who sent down this book, O Muhammad, to you, and sent you to these polytheists as a mercy from your Lord, the Owner of the seven heavens and the earth and what is between them of all things. And His statement: If you are certain means: If you are certain of the truth of what I have told you, that your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, then what I have told you is that God is the One who has these attributes, and that this Qur’an is His revelation, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is His Messenger, is the absolute truth, so be certain of it as you are certain of what you are certain of of the truths of things other than Him.
44:8: And His statement: There is no god but Him means: You people have no god but the Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, so do not worship other than Him, for worship is not appropriate for anyone other than Him, nor is it appropriate for anything other than Him. He gives life and causes death, meaning: He is the One who gives life to whomever He wills, and causes death to whatever He wills of what was alive. And His statement: Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old means: He is your Master and the Master of those of your forefathers who came before you. He says: So this one whose description is like this is the Lord, so worship Him instead of your gods who are unable to harm or benefit.
44:9: And His statement: Rather, they are in doubt, playing. God Almighty says that they are not certain of the truth of what is said to them and what they are told of this report. He is rebuking the polytheists of Quraysh with that, but they are in doubt about it, so they are playing with their doubt about what they are told of it.
44:10: God Almighty means by His saying: Then wait, so wait, O Muhammad, for these polytheists from your people who are in doubt and playing. It is an active verb, from the root word raqabah, meaning if you wait for him and guard him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So wait: meaning, wait. And His statement: On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. The people of interpretation differed about this which God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to await, and informed him that the sky would bring forth a visible al-Dukhan 44:what day it would be, and when it would be, and about the meaning of the smoke that was mentioned in this place. Some of them said: That was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon his Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, against the Quraysh to take them with years like the years of Joseph, so they were afflicted with famine. They said: What was meant by the smoke was what would afflict them at that time in their eyes from the intensity of the hunger and the darkness like the appearance of smoke. It was mentioned that he said that: Isa bin Uthman bin Isa Al-Ramli told me, he said: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: We entered the mosque, and there was a man telling his companions stories, and he said: The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. Do you know what that smoke is? That is a smoke that will come on the Day of Resurrection, and it will take away the hearing and sight of the hypocrites, and it will cause the believers to suffer from something similar to a cold. He said: So we went to Ibn Mas`ud and mentioned that to him, and he was lying down. He was startled, so he sat up and said: God, the Almighty, said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it, nor am I of the pretenders.” [p. 86] It is part of knowledge for a man to say, when he does not know, “God knows best. I will tell you about that. When the Quraysh delayed converting to Islam and resisted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he called upon them to have years like the years of Joseph. They were afflicted with hardship and hunger until they ate bones and dead meat, and they raised their eyes to the sky but saw nothing but smoke. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: “The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, * Enveloping the people. This is a painful punishment.” They said: “Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.” God, the Most High, said: “Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little. Indeed, you will return. * The Day We will strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take revenge.” (al-Dukhan 44:15-16) He said: So they returned on the day of Badr, and He took revenge. God is from them. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said: Malik bin Sa’ir told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: There was a man in the mosque reminding the people, so he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Isa, on the authority of Yahya bin Isa, except that he said: So he took revenge on the day of Badr, so it was the greatest blow. Ibn Humayd and Amr ibn al-Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha Muslim ibn Subayh, on the authority of Masruq, who said: We were sitting with Abdullah ibn Mas`ud and he was lying down among us. A man came to him and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, there is a storyteller at the gates of Kindah, who tells stories and claims that the Sign of the Smoke will come and take the breath away of the disbelievers, and that it will affect the believers like a cold. Abdullah got up and sat down, angry, and said: O people, fear God. Whoever knows something, let him say what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: God knows best. Amr said: It is more beneficial for one of you to say about what he does not know: God knows best. And it does not matter to one of you to say about what he does not know: I do not know. God the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: ‘I do not ask of you for this any reward, nor am I of the pretenders.’” When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the people turning away, he said: O God, seven days like the seven days of Joseph. Then a famine seized them that consumed everything, until they ate skins, dead bodies, and carcasses. One of them looked at the sky and saw smoke from hunger. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb came to him and said: O Muhammad, you have come to command obedience and to maintain kinship ties, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them. God the Almighty said: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.... until His saying: Indeed, you will return. He said: Then He removed from them “the Day We shall strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take revenge.” So the strike was the Day of Badr, and the verse of the Romans and the verse of the smoke, and the strike and the binding had passed. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: Abdullah said: Five have passed: Smoke, Al-Lizam, Al-Batsha, Al-Qamar, and Al-Rum. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Asim, who said: I witnessed a funeral in which Zayd bin Ali was present, and he began to narrate on that day, and he said: The smoke will come before the Day of Resurrection, and it will cause a cold in the nose of the believer, and it will cause the ears of the unbeliever. I said: May God have mercy on you, our companion Abdullah had said something other than this. He said: The smoke has already passed, and he recited this verse: “Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, enveloping the people. This is a painful torment.” He said: The people were afflicted with such hardship that a man could see smoke between him and the sky. That is what he said: Then await. And Abdullah recited it like this until he said: Believers. He said: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little. (17:8) I said to Zayd: So they returned, and God brought Badr back to them. That is what he said: And if you return, We will return. (17:8) So that was the day of Badr. He said: So he accepted, by God. Asim said: A man responded to him, and Zaid, may God have mercy on him, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There will come to you narrators, so whatever agrees with the Qur’an, take it, and whatever is not like that, leave it.’” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he said: The great blow was on the day of Badr, and the smoke had passed. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, who said: I heard Abu Al-Aaliyah say: The smoke has passed. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The smoke continued for years and affected them. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I was told that Ibn Masoud used to say: The smoke has passed, there were years like the years of Joseph. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, he said: drought and the withholding of rain from the infidels of Quraysh, until His saying: Indeed, we are believers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke. He said: Ibn Masoud used to say: The smoke has passed, and there were years like the years of Joseph. “It will cover the people. This is a painful torment.” It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, the matter of the smoke has already passed. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah: On the day when we will strike with the greatest strike, he said: On the day of Badr. Others said: The smoke is a sign of God’s signs, sent to His servants before the Hour comes. It enters the ears of the disbelievers and affects the believers like a cold. They said: It has not yet come, but it will come. It was mentioned that he said that: Wasil bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Jami’, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Al-Mughirah, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Baylaman, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: Smoke comes out and affects the believer like a cold, and it enters the ears of the disbeliever and the hypocrite, until it becomes like a roasted head. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Malekah, who said: I went to Ibn Abbas one day and he said: I did not sleep last night until morning. I said: Why? He said: They said the comet appeared, and I was afraid that smoke might have come down, so I did not sleep until morning. Muhammad bin Buzaie’ told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awf, who said: Al-Hasan said: The smoke remains as one of the signs. When the smoke comes, the unbeliever will blow until it comes out of every one of his ears, and the believer will be seized with a cold. Ibn Bashar told us: Uthman told us, meaning Ibn Al-Haytham, who said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, in a similar manner. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Saeed, he said: Smoke will stir up the people. As for the believer, it will take hold of him like a cold. As for the disbeliever, it will stir up the smoke until it comes out of every nook and cranny of his. He said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: The similitude of the earth on that Day will be like that of a house in which a fire has been lit and in which there is no shortage. Issam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: Sufyan bin Saeed Ath-Thawri narrated to us, he said: Mansour bin Al Mu'tamir narrated to us, on the authority of Rib'i bin Harash, he said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The first signs are the Antichrist, the descent of Jesus son of Mary, and a fire that will emerge from the depths of Aden Abyan, driving the people to the place of assembly, taking a rest with them when they say it, and smoke. Hudhayfah said: O Messenger of God, what is smoke? So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the verse: "The Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, engulfing the people. This is a painful torment." It will fill the space between the east and the west and will remain for forty days and nights. As for the believer, it will afflict him like a cold. As for the disbeliever, he will be like a drunkard, coming out of his nostrils, ears, and anus. Muhammad ibn Awf told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, he said: My father told me, he said: Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your Lord has warned you of three things: the smoke that will take hold of the believer like a cold, and it will take hold of the disbeliever and make him swell until it comes out of every nostril in his body. The second is the beast, and the third is the Antichrist.” The more correct of the two opinions is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that the smoke which God ordered His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to await was the hardship that befell his people because of his supplication against them, as Ibn Mas`ud described it, if the report of Hudhayfah that we mentioned from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that we mentioned is not authentic. Even if it is authentic, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) knows best what God revealed to him, and no one has a statement that is authentically attributed to him. I did not testify to its authenticity because Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-`Asqalani told me that he asked Rawad about this hadith, Did you hear it from Sufyan? He said to him, No. I said to him, Did you read it to him? He said, No. I said to him, Was it read to him while you were present and he acknowledged it? He said, No. I said, Then where did you get it from? He said: Some people brought it to me and showed it to me and said to me: Hear it from us. So they read it to me, then they went and narrated it from me, or something like that. So when I mentioned that, I did not testify to its authenticity. Rather, I said that the statement made by Abdullah ibn Mas`ud is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse, because God, the Most High, threatened the polytheists of Quraysh with smoke, and His statement to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke is in the context of God addressing the polytheists of Quraysh and rebuking them, giving them glad tidings with His statement: “There is no god but He; He gives life and causes death. Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old. * Rather, they are in doubt, playing.” (al-Dukhan 44:8-9) Then He followed that with His statement to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then await the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, as an order from Him to him to be patient until His punishment comes to them and a threat to the polytheists. So since it was a threat to them that He had brought it upon them, it was more likely that He had delayed it from them for others. And then, it is not denied that what he threatened the infidels with this threat was made permissible for them, and that it would be permissible for what is renewed later with others to be smoke, according to what the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have come to us as well, because the reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown that this will happen, since what was narrated from him by Abdullah bin Masoud happened, so both reports that were narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are correct. If the interpretation of the verse in this place is what we have said, then since what we have said in that is the more appropriate of the two interpretations, then it is clear that its meaning is: So wait, O Muhammad, for the polytheists of your people on the day when the sky will bring them the calamity that will befall them because of their disbelief, like smoke, which will be clear to whoever contemplates it that it is smoke.
44:11: People are overwhelmed: He says: Their sight is overwhelmed by the effort that has befallen them. This is a painful torment. Meaning that they say because of the distress and effort that has befallen them: This is a painful torment. It means that the word they say has been omitted from the statement, so that the listeners can know its meaning without mentioning it.
44:12: And His saying: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us means that the unbelievers who are afflicted with that hardship supplicate to their Lord by asking Him to remove that hardship from them, and they say: If You remove it, we will believe in You and worship You without any other deity besides You, as He, the Most High, said about them: “Our Lord, remove the punishment from us. Indeed, we are believers.”
44:13: God Almighty says: How can these polytheists remember after the calamity has befallen them, when they have turned away from Our Messenger when he came to them, not remembering what is recited to them from Our Book, nor taking heed from what he admonishes them with from Our arguments, and saying: He is only a madman who learned this speech. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: How will they be reminded? the people of interpretation said. Mention of the one who said that: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: How will they be reminded? He said: How will they be reminded? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, How can they be reminded? after this calamity has occurred.
44:14: And similar to what we also said in his statement: Then they turned away from him and said, ‘A madman’s teacher,’ the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then they turned away from him and said, ‘A madman’s teacher.’ He said: They turned away from Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and said, A madman’s teacher.
44:15: And His statement: "Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while. Indeed, you will return." God Almighty says to these polytheists about whom He informed that they seek help from Him from the descending smoke and the torment that befell them due to hardship, and He informed that they pledged to Him that if He removed the punishment from them, they would believe. Indeed, We will remove the punishment means the harm that befell them due to the fertility that We create for them. "For a little while. Indeed, you will return." He says: You polytheists, if I remove from you the harm that is upon you, you will not fulfill what you promise and pledge to your Lord of faith, but you will return to your misguidance and error, and you were not before He removed from you. Qatada said: It means: You will return to God’s punishment. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us this, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on his authority. As for those who said that what is meant by His statement, On the Day the sky will bring forth a visible smoke, is the smoke itself, then they said in this passage: What is meant by the torment of which He said, Indeed, We will remove the punishment, is the smoke. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little, meaning the smoke. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little, he said: He did, He removed the smoke when it was. His saying: You will return. He said: He uncovered them and they returned. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: You will return to the punishment of God.
44:16: God the Most High says: “O polytheists, if I remove from you the torment that has descended upon you and the harm that has befallen you, and then you return to your disbelief and break the covenant that you made with your Lord, I will take revenge on you on the Day when I will strike you with My greatest punishment in this world and destroy you.” And God removed the punishment from them, and they returned, so He, the Most High, struck them with His greatest punishment in this world and destroyed them by killing them with the sword. The interpreters differed about the great punishment. Some of them said: It is God’s punishment of the polytheists of Quraysh on the day of Badr. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, that he said: The great blow: the day of Badr. Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri told me, he said: Malik bin Sa’ir told us, he said: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, he said: He said on the day of Badr, the great strike. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Muhammad, he said: I was told that Ibn Mas`ud used to say: The day we strike with the greatest strike is the day of Badr. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, On the day when we strike with the greatest strike, he said: On the day of Badr. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: The Day We shall strike with the greatest strike, he said: The Day of Badr. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, he said: I heard Abu Al-Aaliyah regarding this verse, The Day We strike with the greatest strike, he said: The Day of Badr. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The Day We strike with the greatest strike, indeed, We will take retribution. He said: He means the Day of Badr. Abu Kurayb told us: Uthman bin Ali told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: I said: What is the Greatest Blow? He said: The Day of Resurrection. I said: Abdullah used to say: The Day of Badr. He said: It reached me that he was asked after that and he said: The Day of Badr. Abu Kurayb and Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, he said: On the day of Badr. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: The Day We strike with the greatest strike: the Day of Badr. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: The Day We strike with the greatest strike, he said: This is the Day of Badr. Others said: Rather, it is God’s punishment of His enemies on the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned that he said that: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Khalid Al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Ibn Masoud said: The great blow was on the Day of Badr, and I say: It is on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Kuraib and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Ikrimah passed by me, so I asked him about the great slap. He said: The Day of Resurrection. I said: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud used to say: The Day of Badr. Someone who asked him after that informed me, and he said: The Day of Badr. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: The Day We strike with the greatest strike, Qatada said on the authority of Al-Hasan: It is the Day of Resurrection. We have previously explained the correctness of this, and the reason for which we chose to say what we chose to say about it.
44:17: And His statement: And We certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh means, God Almighty said: And We certainly tested and tried, O Muhammad, before the polytheists of your people, an example of these being the people of Pharaoh from among the Copts. And there came to them a noble messenger means: And there came to them a messenger from Us whom We sent to them, and he is Moses, son of Imran, may God’s prayers be upon him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger, meaning Moses. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: A noble Messenger, he said: Moses, peace be upon him. God Almighty described him as being noble because he was noble to Him and held a high position with Him. It is possible that He described him thus because he was noble and central among his people.
44:18: And His statement: That you deliver to me the servants of God, God Almighty says: And there came to the people of Pharaoh a messenger from God, who was honored by him, saying: Delivere me. The meaning of deliver is: Delivere me, so send with me and follow me. It is similar to His statement: Send with us the Children of Israel. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 17) So in His statement: That you deliver to me, there is an accusative, and the servants of God is an accusative with His statement: Delivere. Some people interpreted it as: Delivere me the servants of God. So, according to this interpretation, the servants of God is an accusative as a vocative. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that they should be brought to me, the people of interpretation said. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And We had certainly tried before them the people of Pharaoh, and there came to them a noble messenger, saying, ‘Give me the servants of God. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.’” He said: He says: Follow me to what I call you to of the truth. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: That you bring to me the servants of God, he said: Send the Children of Israel with me. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: That you bring to me the servants of God. He said: The Children of Israel. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, That you deliver to me the servants of God, meaning the Children of Israel. He said to Pharaoh: Why are you holding back these people, a free people whom you have taken as slaves? Let them go. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: That you deliver to me the servants of God, he said: He says: Send the servants of God with me, meaning the Children of Israel, and he recited: Then send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them (Ta-Ha: 47). He said: That is His statement: That you deliver to me the servants of God, he said: Return them to us. And His saying: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger means: I am to you, O people, a messenger from God who has sent me to you. His punishment will not overtake you because of your disbelief in Him. Trustworthy means: Trustworthy in His revelation and His message that He promised me to you.
44:19: God Almighty says: And there came to them a noble Messenger, [saying], Come to me, servants of God, and do not exalt yourselves above God. What he meant by his saying: That you do not exalt yourselves above God is that you do not transgress and rebel against your Lord, so that you disbelieve in Him and disobey Him, and thus go against His command. Indeed, I come to you with clear authority. He says: I come to you with proof of the truth of what I am calling you to, and evidence of its correctness, clear to whoever contemplates and ponders it that it is my proof of the correctness of what I am saying to you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And do not exalt yourselves over God: meaning do not seek to transgress against God. Indeed, I come to you with clear authority: meaning with a clear excuse. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, in a similar manner. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And do not exalt yourselves over God means: Do not fabricate lies about God.
44:20: And His saying: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord, lest you stone me. He says: And I have taken refuge in my Lord and your Lord, and I have sought protection in Him from you, lest you stone me. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the stoning from which the Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, sought refuge with his Lord. Some of them said: It is verbal abuse. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from being stoned by you, he said: He means stoning the speech. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Uthman bin Omar bin Faris told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from being stoned by you, he said: Stoning means by word. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me. He said: That you say he is a magician. Others said: Rather, it is stoning. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from being stoned: meaning that you are stoned. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: That you stone me. He said: That you stone me with stones. Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying that you stone is that you kill me. The first of the opinions on this matter is what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the words, which is that Moses, peace be upon him, sought refuge with God from being stoned by Pharaoh and his people. Stoning may be a verbal statement or an action with the hand. The correct view is: Moses sought refuge with his Lord from every meaning of their stoning, which would cause harm and distress to the one being stoned, whether it be verbal abuse or stoning with the hand.
44:21: And His statement: And if you do not believe in me, then leave me. God Almighty says, informing about what His Prophet Moses, peace be upon him, said to Pharaoh and his al-Nas 114:And if you, O people, do not believe in what I have brought you from my Lord, then leave me. He says: Leave me alone, without being stoned by tongue or hand. Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And if you do not believe in me, then leave me alone: meaning, leave me alone.
44:22: God Almighty says: So Moses called upon his Lord when they denied him and did not believe in him, and did not bring the servants of God to him, and intended to kill him, because these, meaning Pharaoh and his people, are a criminal people, meaning: that they are polytheists and disbelievers in God.
44:23: And His statement: So travel by night with My servants. There is an omission in the speech that is sufficient in its indication of what was mentioned, which is: So his Lord answered him by saying to him: So travel by night, since the matter is thus, with My servants, and they are the Children of Israel. The meaning of the speech is: So travel by night with My servants who believed in you and believed in you and followed you, not those among them who disbelieved in you and refused to accept the advice you brought them, and those who were of this nature on that day were the Children of Israel. And He said: So travel by night with My servants, because the meaning of that is: Travel with them at night before morning. His saying: You will be pursued means: Pharaoh and his Copts will pursue you if you leave their country and their land in your footsteps.
44:24: And His statement: And leave the sea at ease means: If you and your companions cross the sea, leave it calm as it was when you entered it. It was said that God, the Exalted, said this to Moses after he crossed the sea with the Children of Israel. Since that was the case, then there is an omission in the statement, which is: So Moses traveled with My servants by night, and crossed the sea with them. So We said to him after he crossed it, and he wanted to return the sea to its condition before it split: Leave it at ease. It was mentioned that God Almighty said to Moses, peace be upon him, this statement after he crossed the sea with his people: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: So he called upon his Lord, ‘Indeed, these are a criminal people,’ until he reached Indeed, they are a drowned army. He said: When the last of the Children of Israel left, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to strike the sea with his staff so that it would return to what it was, for fear that the people of Pharaoh would overtake them, but it was said to him, Leave the sea alone, for they are a drowned army. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: When he had crossed the sea, he turned to strike the sea with his staff so that it would reunite, and he was afraid that Pharaoh and his soldiers would follow him, so he was told: Leave the sea alone as it is, for they are a drowned army. The interpreters differed about the meaning of rahwa. Some of them said: It means: Leave it as it was. Mention of the one who said that: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And leave the sea at ease means: in a straight line. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: “And leave the sea in tranquility. Indeed, they are a drowned host.” He said: Temptation means that you leave it as it was, for they will not be saved from behind it. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hamid told us, on the authority of Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of his father, that Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b about the statement of God, “And leave the sea in peace,” he said: A path. Others said: Rather, it means: Leave it easy. It was mentioned that he said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, his saying: And leave the sea at ease, he said: Easy. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And leave the sea at ease. He said: It is said: At ease means a plain. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Harami bin Ammarah told us: Shu’bah told us: Ammarah told me on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And leave the sea at ease, he said: Gentle. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And leave the sea at ease, he said: Easy and pleasant. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And leave the sea at ease, he said: It is the plain. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Leave it dry and new. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ubaidullah bin Muadh told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And leave the sea at ease, he said: Fresh. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ubayd God ibn Muadh told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And leave the sea at rest, he said: Dry, as it was after you struck it. He said: Do not order it to return, leave it until the last of them enters. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: a path of ease, he said: a dry path. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And leave the sea as a path, as it is, a dry road. The most correct of the sayings about this is the one that says that its meaning is: Leave it as it was when you took it. This is because in the speech of the Arabs, raho means stillness, as the poet said: As if the people of Hajar were watching when they saw me outside, a singing bird. A bird saw a hawk dripping with blood, and its mother went out to Eid That is, at rest. If that is what it means, then there is no doubt that it was left easy and smooth, and a dry path, because the Children of Israel crossed it when they crossed it, and it was like that. So if the sea was left calm as it was when Moses crossed it, calm and not agitated, then there is no doubt that it was in the manner described. His saying: They are a drowned army means: Pharaoh and his people are God’s army who will be drowned in the sea.
44:25: God Almighty says: How many gardens and trees did Pharaoh and his people leave behind among the Copts after their destruction and God drowning them, and springs, meaning: and sources of what used to gush forth in their gardens and crops standing in their farms.
44:26: And a noble position He says: And a noble and noble position they used to occupy. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of God’s description of that station as generous. Some of them said: He described it thus because of its honor, and that is because it is the station of kings and princes. They said: What is meant by it is the pulpits. Mention of the one who said that: Jaafar Ibn Bint Ishaq Al-Azraq told me, he said: Saeed Ibn Muhammad Al-Thaqafi told us, he said: Ismail Ibn Ibrahim Ibn Muhajir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And a noble station, he said: The pulpits. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me, he said: Abdullah bin Dawud Al-Wasiti told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement: And a noble station, he said: The pulpits. Others said: He described that place as generous because of its beauty and splendor. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And a noble station means: good.
44:27: And His statement: And they were brought out of a blessing in which they were enjoying themselves. God Almighty says: And they were brought out of a blessing in which they were enjoying themselves, reveling in it, and enjoying it. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase fakihin. Most of the regions except Abu Ja`far al-Qari` read it fakihin with the meaning I described. Abu Raja` al-`Attardi, al-Hasan, and Abu Ja`far al-Madani read it fakihin meaning: arrogant and haughty. The correct reading in my opinion is the reading used by the readers of the regions, which is fakihin with an alif, meaning soft. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And they were enjoying pleasure in it: comfortable. He said: Yes, by God, God expelled him from his gardens, his springs, and his crops until He threw him into the sea.
44:28: And His statement: Likewise, We caused another people to inherit it. God Almighty says: Thus, as I have described to you, O people, We did with those whose affair I have mentioned to you, who denied Our Messenger Moses, peace and blessings be upon him. And His statement: And We caused another people to inherit it, God Almighty says: And We caused their gardens, springs, crops, dwellings, and whatever blessings they had enjoyed to be inherited from them to another people after their destruction. It was said that what is meant by the other people are the Children of Israel. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Likewise, and We caused another people to inherit it, meaning the Children of Israel.
44:29: God Almighty says: So neither the heavens nor the earth wept for those whom God drowned in the sea, namely Pharaoh and his people. It has been said that the weeping of the heavens is the redness of its edges. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told me, he said: Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Hammad told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Zuhair, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: When Al-Hussein bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, was killed, the sky wept for him, and its weeping was its redness. Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, he said: Its weeping is the redness of its edges. It was said: The heavens and the earth did not weep for them is because when a believer dies, the heavens and the earth weep for him for forty mornings, but they did not weep for Pharaoh and his people, because they had no good deeds that would ascend to God, so the heavens would weep for them, nor any mosque on earth, so the earth would weep for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Those who said that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq bin Ghanam narrated to us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Minhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: O Abu Abbas, tell me about the statement of God, the Most High: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved. Do the heavens and the earth weep for anyone? He said: Yes, there is no one among creation but that he has a door in the heaven from which his provision descends and through which his deeds ascend. So when a believer dies and his door in the heaven through which his deeds ascended and his provision descended is closed, he is wept for. And when his place of prayer is lost in the land in which he used to pray and remember God, he is wept for. The people of Pharaoh had no good traces on the earth, and no good ascended from them to the heaven. He said: So the heavens and the earth did not weep for them. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman and Yahya told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It was said: The earth weeps over the believer for forty mornings. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya al-Qattat, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Yahya bin Talha told me: Fadil bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was told that when a believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings. Ibn Bashar told us: Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami told us: Bakir ibn Abi al-Sumait told us: Qatada told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, that he used to say: The regions of the earth from which his deeds ascend to the heavens weep for him after his death, meaning the believer. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them. He said: There is no one but that he has a door in the heaven through which his provision descends and through which his deeds ascend. Then, when he loses it, the places where he used to prostrate weep for him. And the people of Pharaoh did not have any righteous deeds on earth that would be accepted from them, so that they would ascend to God Almighty. So Mujahid said: The earth weeps for the believer for forty mornings. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It was said: When a believer dies, the earth weeps over him for forty mornings. Yahya bin Talha narrated: Isa bin Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Safwan bin Amr, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubaid Al-Hadrami, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange. There is no strangeness for the believer. No believer dies in a foreign land in which his mourners are absent from him, but the heavens and the earth weep for him.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And neither the heavens nor the earth wept for them,’ then he said: ‘They do not weep for the disbeliever.’” Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them… the verse. He said: That is because there is no believer on earth who dies except that the mosques in which he used to pray weep for him when they lose him, and except that the place in heaven from which his words were raised weeps for him. That is what He said to the people who disobeyed Him: And neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, nor were they reprieved. Because they weep for the friends of God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, meaning: The heaven and the earth do not weep for the disbeliever, but they weep for the righteous believer, whose landmarks are on the earth and whose place of work is in the heavens. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: So neither the heaven nor the earth wept for them, he said: The parts of the earth on which the believer used to pray weep for him when he died, and the parts of the heavens in which his deeds were raised. Ibn Hamid narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked: Do the heavens and the earth weep for anyone? He said: Yes, there is no one among creation except that he has a door in the heaven through which his deeds ascend and from which his provision descends. So when he dies, his place on earth where he used to remember God and pray weeps for him, and his door through which his deeds ascended and from which his provision descended weeps for him. As for the people of Pharaoh, they had no good deeds, and no good thing ascended to the heavens from them, so the heavens and the earth did not weep for them. His statement: And they were not given respite means: They were not delayed in the punishment that befell them, but they were hastened to it when they angered their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, with them.
44:30: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment: God Almighty says: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the punishment with which Pharaoh and his people were tormenting them. Humiliating means humiliating them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating punishment by killing their sons and keeping their women alive.
44:31: And His statement: "From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors." God the Almighty says: And We had certainly saved the Children of Israel from the punishment from Pharaoh. So His statement: From Pharaoh is a repetition of His statement: From the humiliating punishment, a substitution of the first. What is meant by His statement: Indeed, he was haughty and among the transgressors is that he was a tyrant, haughty and arrogant towards his Lord. Of the transgressors means: of those who transgressed beyond what they should not transgress. Rather, God the Almighty means that he was aggressive in his disbelief and arrogant towards his Lord the Almighty.
44:32: God Almighty says: And We chose the Children of Israel, with knowledge from Us, over the people of their time at that time, and that was the time of Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds: meaning they were chosen over the people of their time, and every time has a scholar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds, he said: The world of that time. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We chose them with knowledge over the worlds, he said: over those who were among them.
44:33: His statement: And We gave them signs in which there was a clear trial. God Almighty says: And We gave them lessons and morals in which there was a test, which makes clear to whoever contemplates it that it was a test with which God tested them. The interpreters differed regarding this affliction. Some of them said: He afflicted them with His blessings upon them. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And We gave them signs in which there was clear trial means that God saved them from their enemy, then He cut off the sea for them, shaded them with clouds, and sent down upon them manna and quails. Others said: Rather, He tested them with ease and hardship. It was mentioned that he said that: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And We gave them of the signs that which was a clear trial, and he recited: And We test you with evil and with good as trial, and to Us you will be returned. (Al-Anbiya’: 35) and he said: A clear trial for whoever believed in it and disbelieved in it, a trial with which We test them, We purify them with a trial of testing, We test them with good and evil, We test them to see from what He gave them of the signs who will believe in it, benefit from it and waste it. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God informed us that He gave the Children of Israel signs that would test and try them. The test and trial may be in ease or in hardship, and He did not provide us with evidence from the report or reason that He meant some of that and not others. God tested them with both meanings together. It is possible that He meant that He tested them with both of them. If the matter is as we have described, then the correct thing to say about it is as God, the Most High, said that He tested them.
44:34: God Almighty says, informing us of what the polytheists of Quraysh said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: These polytheists from your people, O Muhammad, say, ‘It is only our first death,’ which we will die, and it is the first death.
44:35: And we will not be resurrected after our death, nor will we be sent forth, as a denial from them of resurrection, reward, and punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “Indeed, these people say: ‘There is only our first death, and we will not be resurrected.’” He said: The polytheists of the Arabs said: And we will not be resurrected, meaning: they will not be resurrected.
44:36: And His statement: Then bring our fathers, if you should be truthful. God Almighty says: They said to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Then bring our fathers who have died, if you should be truthful, that God will raise us up after our trial in our graves, and revive us after our death. And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was addressed, and he alone is addressed to everyone, as it was said: O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1) and as He said: My Lord, send me back (al-Mu’minun 23:99). And I have explained that in more than one place in our book.
44:37: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Are these polytheists, O Muhammad, better than your people, or the people of Tubba’, meaning Tubba’ al-Himyari? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Are they better or the people of Tubba’? He said: The Himyarites. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Are they better, the people of Tubba’? He told us that the people of Tubba’ were a man from Himyar, he marched with armies until he bewildered Al-Hirah, then he came to Samarkand and destroyed it. He told us that if he wrote in the name of the one he called himself and ruled over land and sea, health and wind. He told us that Ka’b used to say: Describe the description of the righteous man, God will blame his people with a blame that he blames him. Aisha used to say: Do not curse Tubba’, for he was a righteous man. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Aisha said: Tubba' was a righteous man. Ka'b said: God condemned his people, but He did not condemn him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Tamim ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, that Tubba’ covered the Kaaba. Sa’id forbade cursing it. And His statement: And those before them means that God Almighty says: Are these polytheists from Quraysh better or the people of Tubba and those before them from the nations who disbelieved in their Lord? He says: These are not better than those, so we should pardon them and not destroy them, and they are disbelievers in God, just as those nations before them whom We destroyed were disbelievers. His statement: Indeed, they were criminals means: The people of Tubba’ and those before them of the nations whom We destroyed, We only destroyed them because of their crimes and their disbelief in their Lord. It was said: They were criminals, so the alif of in was broken as a starting point, and it has the meaning of a condition, as the speech does not indicate its meaning.
44:38: God Almighty says: And We did not create the seven heavens and the earths and everything between them in play.
44:39: And His statement: We did not create them except with the truth means: We did not create the heavens and the earth except with the truth without which management is not valid. And by that, the Most High means to point out the truth of resurrection and recompense. The Most High says: We did not create the creation in vain, by bringing them to life as We willed, then annihilating them without testing them with obedience, commands and prohibitions, and without rewarding the obedient for his obedience, and the disobedient for his disobedience. Rather, We created this to test whomever We willed to test from among Our creation with whatever test We willed of commands and prohibitions. That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness. (al-Najm 53:31) But most of them do not know. God Almighty says: But most of these polytheists do not know that God created for them, so they do not fear God’s wrath as punishment for what they do, nor do they expect any good reward for what they do, because of their denial of the afterlife.
44:40: God Almighty says: The Day God will judge between His creation for what they did in this world of good or evil, He will reward the doer of good with good, and the doer of evil with evil. A time for them all together: He says: A time for their gathering all together. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all is the day on which people will be judged by their deeds.
44:41: And His statement: On the Day when no protector will avail another protector at all, meaning: no cousin will ward off another cousin, nor a friend from his friend, from anything of the punishment that has befallen them from God. Nor will they be aided, meaning: nor will they aid one another, so they seek refuge from whoever has afflicted them with punishment, as they used to do in this world. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: On the Day when no protector will avail another at all… the verse, on that Day, O son of Adam, all causes will be cut off, and people will return to their deeds. So whoever attains good on that Day will be happy with it as a final consequence of his deeds, and whoever attains evil on that Day will be miserable with it as a final consequence of his deeds.
44:42: And his statement: Except for whom God has mercy The Arab scholars differed regarding the position of <of>in his statement: Except for whom God has mercy, so some of the grammarians of Basra said: Except for whom God has mercy, so he made it a substitute for the implied noun in they will be helped, and if you wish you can make it the subject and implied its predicate, meaning: Except for whom God has mercy, so it will suffice. And some of the grammarians of Kufa said: His statement: Except for whom God has mercy, he said: The believers intercede for one another, so if you wish you can make <of>in the nominative case, as if you said: No one can stand except so-and-so, and if you wish you can make it the accusative as an exception and a break from the beginning of the sentence, meaning: O God, except for whom God has mercy. Others among them said: Its meaning is: A master cannot avail another master at all, except for someone whom God has given permission to intercede. He said: It cannot be a substitute for what is in they will be helped, because except is definite, the first is negated, and a substitute can only have the meaning of the first. He said: Likewise, it is not permissible for it to be a new sentence, because it cannot be a new sentence with an exception. The most correct of the sayings about this is that it is in the nominative case, meaning: On the Day when no protector will avail another protector at all, except for those upon whom God has mercy, for He will avail him by interceding for him with his Lord. And His saying: Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful. God Almighty says, describing Himself: Indeed, God is the Exalted in His vengeance against His enemies, the Merciful to His friends and those who obey Him.
44:43: God the Most High says: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum which He informed us grows at the bottom of Hell, which He made food for the people of Hell, its fruit in Hell is the food of the sinner in this world with regard to his Lord. The sinner is the one who commits sin, and sin comes from athama to sin, meaning to be sinful, so he is athim atheem. What is meant by it here is the one whose sin is disbelief in his Lord, not any other sin.
44:44: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam bin al-Harith, that Abu al-Darda’ was teaching a man, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is food for the sinner, and he said, Food for the orphan, so Abu al-Darda’ said, Say, ‘Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * is food for the wicked.’ Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If a drop of the Zaqqum of Hell were sent down to the world, it would ruin people’s livelihood. Abu al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam, who said: Abu al-Darda’ was teaching a man, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful. The man kept saying, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the orphan. When Abu al-Darda’ continued to repeat this verse, he saw that he did not understand, so he said, Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum is food for the sinful, he said: Abu Jahl.
44:45: And His statement: Like boiling molten metal in the bellies, God Almighty says: The tree of Zaqqum, whose fruit is made the food of the disbeliever in Hell, is like lead or silver, or what is melted in fire when it is melted in it, so its heat is extreme, and its rage is intense in the intense blackness. We have previously explained the meaning of the term period of grace in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here in this context, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among the scholars of interpretation regarding it. However, we will mention from the statements of the scholars in this context what we did not mention there. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about the statement of God, the Most High, like molten copper. He said: Like the dregs of oil. Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Like boiling oil in the bellies, meaning: black like boiling oil. Abu Kurayb, Abu al-Sa’ib, and Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: like molten metal: thick water like the dregs of oil. Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abd Al-Samad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, he said: Khalid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he saw silver that had been melted, and he said: This is the molten metal. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, he said: Amr bin Maymun told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement: Like molten copper that scorcheth faces (al-Kahf 18:29), he said: Abdullah entered the treasury, and brought out some remains that were in it, and lit a fire over them until they sparkled. He said: Where is the one who asked about the molten copper? This is the molten copper. Ibn Bashar narrated: Ibn Abi Uday narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated: Awf narrated: al-Hasan narrated: It reached me that Ibn Mas`ud was asked about the molten metal which they say on the Day of Resurrection is the drink of the people of Hell, and which is under the control of the public treasury. He said: So he called for gold and silver and melted them and said: This is the most similar thing in this world to the molten metal which is the color of the sky on the Day of Resurrection and the drink of the people of Hell, except that it is hotter than this. The wording of the hadith is from Ibn Bashar, and the hadith of Ibn al-Muthanna is similar. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Ash’ath told us, on the authority of al-Hasan: Among his words was that Abdullah ibn Mas’ud was a man whom God had honoured by allowing him to be a companion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar, may God be pleased with him, appointed him over the treasury. He said: So he took a large amount of broken silver and dug a trench for it. Then he ordered a large amount of firewood to be brought and lit a fire over it. When it bubbled and foamed and changed into various colours, he said: Look who is at the door. So he brought the people in and said to them: This is the most similar thing we have ever seen in the world to molten metal. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum * Is food for the sinful… the verse. It was mentioned to us that Ibn Masoud was given a gift of a water trough made of gold and silver, so he ordered that a trench be dug in the ground, then large pieces of firewood were thrown into it, then that water trough was thrown into it, until it foamed and dissolved. He said to his servant: Call whoever is present with us from the people of Kufa. So he called a group, and when they entered he said: Do you see this? They said: Yes.
