He said: We have not seen in the world anything similar to molten metal closer than this gold and silver when it foams and dissolves. Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sufyan Al-Asadi, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud melted silver, then said: Whoever wants to look at the molten metal, let him look at this. Bishr told us: Yazid told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: On the Day when the sky will be like molten copper (al-Ma’arij 70:8), he said: Like the dregs of oil. Yahya bin Talha told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed: Like the dregs of oil. He said: Like the dregs of oil. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ya`mar bin Bishr told us: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us: Abu Al-Sabah told us: I heard Yazid bin Abi Sumayyah say: I heard Ibn Umar say: Do you know what Mahl is? Mahl is the end of the oil, meaning its end. He said: Ibrahim Abu Ishaq al-Talaqani told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, he said: Abu al-Sabah al-Ayli told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Sumayyah, on the authority of Ibn Umar, something similar. Abu Kurayb told us: Rashdin bin Saad told us, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj Abi Al-Samh, on the authority of Abi Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abi Saeed, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: ‘with water like molten brass’ (al-Kahf 18:29), like cloudy oil. So if he brings it close to his face, the scalp of his face falls into it.” He said: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ya`mar bin Bishr told us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, he said: Rashdin bin Sa`d told us, he said: Amr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Abu Al-Samh, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. His saying: in the bellies. The reciters differed in their recitation of that. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Basra, and Kufa recited it as tughli with a ta’, meaning that the tree of Zaqqum was boiling in their bellies. They feminized tughli because of the feminization of the tree. Some of the reciters of Ahl al-Kafwah recited that as well.
44:46: Boils means: the food of the sinner boils, or the boiling pot boils. Some of them mentioned it to remind people of the food, and they interpreted its meaning to mean that the food is what boils in their stomachs. Some of them mentioned it to remind people of the boiling pot, and they interpreted it to mean that it is an attribute of the boiling pot. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings with correct meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. Like the boiling of scalding water means: It boils in the bellies of these wretched people like the boiling of scalding water, which is heated water that has been lit until it reaches the peak of its heat. It was also said to be scalding water and it is scalding, because it is changed from maf’ul to fa’il, just as it is said qatil, from maqtul.
44:47: The Almighty says: Take him, meaning this sinner with his Lord, about whom the Most High has informed us that the tree of Zaqqum is food. Then ascend him, the Almighty says: Push him and drive him. It is said from this: Atala ya’talahu ‘atlan: if he drives him by pushing and pulling. From this is the saying of Al-Farazdaq: The generous are not like your father until you return to Atiya It is pushed and pulled. His statement, to the middle of Hellfire, means to the middle of Hellfire. The meaning of the statement is that it will be said on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Take this sinner and drive him, pushing him on his back and dragging him to the middle of the Fire. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying: So they climbed on him, the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Take him and throw him into the midst of Hellfire, he said: Take him and push him. In his saying: So they ascended it, there are two pronunciations: breaking the ta, which is the reading of some of the people of Medina and some of the people of Mecca. The correct reading of this, according to us, is that they are two dialects in Arabic, and it is said: ‘Atal, Ya’tal, and Ya’tal. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: To the middle of Hellfire means to the middle of the fire.
44:48: And His statement: Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water. God Almighty says: Then they poured over this sinner’s head the torment of scalding water, meaning: the heated water whose description we have described, and which is the water about which God said, With it will melt what is in their bellies and their skins, and its description has been explained there.
44:49: God Almighty says: It will be said to this sinful, wretched person: Taste this torment with which you are being tormented today. Indeed, you are the honorable one among your people, the generous one over them. He mentioned that these verses were revealed about Abu Jahl bin Hisham. Those who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Then they poured over his head the torment of scalding water. This was revealed about the enemy of God, Abu Jahl. “He met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he seized him and shook him, then he said: ‘It is more fitting for you, O Abu Jahl, then it is more fitting for you, then it is more fitting for you. Taste that you are the mighty and noble.’ That is because he said: ‘Does Muhammad promise me? By God, I am more mighty than anyone who walked between two mountains.” This is also the case with And do not obey any sinner or ungrateful among them. (al-Insan 76:24), and this is also the case with No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near. (al-Alaq 96:19) Qatada said: This was revealed about Abu Jahl and his companions whom God, the Blessed and Exalted, killed on the day of Badr. Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and settled their people in the home of destruction? (Ibrahim 14:28). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Seize him and ascend him was revealed about Abu Jahl. Qatada said: Abu Jahl said: There is no man between the two mountains more honorable or more generous than me. So God Almighty said: Taste, for you are the honorable, the generous. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Take him and throw him into the midst of Hellfire, he said: This is for Abu Jahl. If someone were to say: How could it be said, while he is being humiliated with the torment mentioned by God, and is being humbled by violence to the level of Hellfire: You are the Exalted, the Generous? It would be said: His saying: You are the Exalted, the Generous is not a description of the one who said that to him with honor and generosity, but rather it is an appreciation from him for what he used to describe himself with in this world, and a rebuke to him with that in the form of a narrative, because in this world he used to say: You are the Exalted, the Generous, so it would be said to him in the Hereafter, when he is tormented with what he was tormented with in the Fire: “Taste this humiliation today, for you used to claim that you were the Exalted, the Generous, and that you were the one who was humiliated and degraded. So where is that which you used to say and claim of honor and generosity? Why do you not protect yourself from the torment with your honor?” Ibn Bashar narrated: Sufyan ibn Isa narrated: Ibn Ajlan narrated from Saeed Al-Maqburi from Abu Hurairah who said: Kaab said: God has three garments: He wraps Himself in glory, He dresses Himself in mercy, and He wears the garment of majesty. Exalted is He. Whoever is proud of something other than that which God has honored him with, he is the one for whom it is said: Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. Whoever is merciful to people, he is the one for whom God has clothed himself in the garment that befits him. Whoever is arrogant, he is the one who has disputed with God over His cloak. God, the Exalted, says: It is not fitting for one who disputes with Me over My cloak that I should admit him to Paradise. The Qur’an reciters of all regions unanimously agreed to pronounce the alif in the phrase Think, for you with a kasra as a starting point. And the account of the saying of this speaker: I am the mighty, the generous. Some of the later scholars read it as Think, for you with a fatha on the alif, based on the word Think in the phrase for you, as if the meaning of the statement to him was: Taste this statement that you said in this world. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is to break the alif of inka according to the meaning that I mentioned to its reader, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it, and the anomaly of what contradicts it. And sufficient evidence of the error of a reading contrary to it is what the imams of the past and present have followed, despite its distance from correctness in meaning and its separation from the interpretation of the people of interpretation.
44:50: And His statement: This is what you were in doubt about, God Almighty says: It will be said to him: This torment with which you are being tormented today is the torment about which you were in doubt in this world, and about which you disputed, and about which you were not certain. You have encountered it, so taste it.
44:51: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who fear Him by performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience in a place of residence, are safe in that place from what they feared in the stations of this world of afflictions, illnesses, calamities, and sorrows. The reciters differed in their reading of the phrase: in the place of a trustworthy person. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as in the place of a trustworthy person with a damma on the meem, meaning: in the residence of a trustworthy person during the journey. The majority of the reciters of Egypt, Kufa and Basra, read it as in a place with a fatha on the meem, with the meaning we have described, and indicating that they are in the place and position of a trustworthy person. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two widely used readings in the readings of the regions, and their meanings are correct. So whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure position Yes, by God, secure from Satan, idols, and sorrows.
44:52: And his saying: In gardens and springs. The gardens and springs are a translation of the secure station, and the secure station is the gardens and springs, and the gardens are the orchards, and the springs are the springs of water flowing continuously at the roots of the trees of the gardens.
44:53: And His statement: They will wear fine silk, meaning: These righteous people will wear fine silk in these gardens, which is the finest type of brocade, and heavy brocade, which is the thickest type of brocade. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: Of fine silk and heavy brocade, he said: Heavy brocade is thick silk. It was said: They will wear fine silk and brocade, and he did not say clothing, as the meaning of the words is sufficient. His saying: Facing each other means that in Paradise they will face each other, and they will not look at each other’s backs. We have mentioned the narration about that previously, so there is no need to repeat it.
44:54: God Almighty says: Just as We have given these righteous people honor in the Hereafter by admitting them into the Gardens and dressing them therein in fine silk and brocade, likewise We have honored them by also marrying them therein to houris from among the women, who are pure white, and their singular is: houri. Mujahid used to say about the meaning of the houris: Muhammad bin Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, and Al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa’ both narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We shall marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes, he said: We married them to fair women. He said: The fair women are those whom the eye is dazzled by, the marrow of their shins is visible from behind their clothes, and the observer sees his face in the liver of one of them like a mirror because of the thinness of their skin and the purity of their complexion. What Mujahid said, that the meaning of fair women is that which the eye is dazzled by, is a statement that has no meaning in Arabic speech, because fair women is the plural of houri, just as humr is the plural of hamra’, and as-sawd is the plural of sawda’, and hawra’ is a verbal noun from hawra, which means pure whiteness, just as the pure whiteness of food is called hawari. We have explained the meaning of that with supporting evidence previously. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Thus, We will marry them to fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes. He said: White, beautiful eyes. He said: And in Ibn Masoud’s reading: with fair maidens with large, beautiful eyes. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Hoor with wide eyes, he said: White with wide eyes. He said: And in the version of Ibn Mas’ud: Ba’ees with wide eyes. Ibn Mas’ud recited this, meaning that the meaning of Hoor is not the one that Mujahid went with, because Ays among the Arabs is the plural of Aysa, which is the white camel, as al-A’sha said: The mission of a displaced person, the wolves howl at him, cost Aais a cawing under the man By A’is he means: a white camel. As for Ain, it is the plural of Aynaa, which is a woman with large eyes.
44:55: And His statement, They will call therein... the verse, means: These righteous people will call therein for every type of fruit of Paradise that they desire, safe therein from its being cut off from them, running out, or vanishing, and from the harm and evil that it causes. He means: That fruit there is not like the fruit of this world that we eat, and they fear the evil consequences of it, and the aftermath of its harm, even though it will run out from them, and become non-existent at some times and periods. Qatada directed the interpretation of his saying: safe to what: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They will call therein for every kind of fruit, safe and sound. They will be safe from death, illness, and Satan.
44:56: And His statement: They will not taste death therein except the first death. God Almighty says: These righteous people will not taste death in Paradise after the first death that they tasted in this world. Some Arab scholars interpreted the word except in this context to mean except and said: The meaning of the statement is: They will not taste death therein except the first death. He gives an example of this with the words of God Almighty: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred (An-Nisa’: 22), meaning: except what your fathers have done. What he said has no clear basis in my opinion, because what is most likely when someone says: I will not taste food today except the food I tasted before today is that he means to inform the speaker that he has food on that day that he will taste and eat, unlike all other foods. If this is the most likely meaning, then it must have been proven by his words: Except the first death that it is a death of the same type as the first death, which they will taste. It is known that this is not the case, because God Almighty has made the people of Paradise safe in Paradise if they enter it from death, but its meaning is as I have described. It is permissible to put <except>in place of <after>because their meanings are close in this context. That is because if a speaker says: I will not speak to a man today except a man with Amr, he has obligated himself not to speak to a man that day after speaking to the man with Amr. Likewise, if he says: I will not speak to a man today after a man with Amr, he has obligated himself not to speak to a man that day except a man with Amr. So after and except are close in meaning in this context. It is the custom of the Arabs to put one word in place of another if their meanings are close, like putting hope in place of fear because of the fear in the meaning of hope, because hope is not certainty, but rather greed, and it may be true or false, just as fear sometimes comes true and sometimes lies. So, in this regard, Aw Dhu’ayb said: If a wasp stings him, he will not be stung by it, and he will oppose it in the house of Nubb factors He said: He did not fear its sting, meaning: He did not fear its sting. And they put suspicion in place of knowledge that was not perceived by sight, but was perceived by inference or report, as the poet said: I told them that they thought that two thousand armed men were their leaders in the Persian armor. Meaning: Be certain of two thousand armed men and know. So assumption was put in place of certainty if those to whom that was said had not witnessed two thousand armed men, nor seen them, and what this informant had informed them of, so he said to them, assume knowledge of what has not been witnessed is an action of the heart. So one was put in place of the other because their meanings are close in similarities to what I have mentioned, the enumeration of which is great. Just as the meanings of the two words are close in some meanings. They have different meanings in other things, so the Arabs place one of them in place of the other in the place where their meanings are close. Likewise, His statement, They will not taste death therein except the first death, He placed except in place of after because we describe the closeness of the meaning of except and after in this place. Likewise, And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred (An-Nisa’: 22), its meaning is: after what occurred from you in the pre-Islamic period. But if except is directed in this place to the meaning of except, then it is a translation of the place, and an explanation of it with what is more confusing for whoever wants to know its meaning from it.
44:57: And His statement: And He will protect them from the punishment of Hellfire, as a favor from your Lord. God Almighty says: And these righteous people will be protected by their Lord on that Day from the punishment of Hellfire, as a favor from your Lord, O Muhammad, and as a kindness from Him to them thereby. He will not punish them for a crime they committed in the past in this world. And were it not for His favor to them by pardoning them for their past punishment, He would not have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire, but its pain and distress would have reached them and afflicted them. And His statement: That is the great attainment. God Almighty says: This which We have given to these righteous people in the Hereafter of honor that is described in these verses, is the great attainment. He says: It is the great victory in what they sought to attain in this world through their deeds and obedience to their Lord, and their fear of Him, in what He tested them with of acts of obedience and obligations, and avoidance of forbidden things.
44:58: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have only made easy the recitation of this Qur’an which We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, in your language, so that these polytheists to whom We have sent you may remember its lessons and arguments, and be admonished by its sermons, and reflect on its verses when you recite it to them, so that they may return to the obedience of their Lord, and submit to the truth when it becomes clear to them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: We have only made it easy in your language: meaning this Qur’an that they may remember. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: We have only made it easy for your tongue, he said: the Qur’an, and We made it easy: He set his tongue at ease with it.
44:59: And His saying: So wait, for they are waiting. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So wait, O Muhammad, for the victory from your Lord, and the victory over these polytheists among your people from Quraysh, for they are waiting in their hearts for your subjugation and your dominance by turning away from the truth that you have brought them, whoever wants to accept it and follow you in it. And in a manner similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: Then wait, for they are waiting, the people of interpretation said. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then wait, for they are waiting. That is, wait, for they are waiting.
